events.title: Perl 5.0 released
events.summary: Larry Wall released Perl 5.0 on October 17, 1994 — a complete rewrite adding objects, references, modules, and the CPAN ecosystem foundation.
events.about: Perl 5 became the duct tape of the early web: CGI scripts, system administration, bioinformatics, and text munging. The module system and CPAN let developers share libraries decades before npm or PyPI — powering everything from Slashdot to early Amazon glue code.

narrative.whyChosen: Perl 5 defined scripting culture for the 1990s web and Unix automation.
narrative.whyImportant: Objects, references, and CPAN made Perl a platform, not just a language.
narrative.problemSolved: Perl 4 could not scale to complex programs; the web needed a richer scripting language with reusable libraries.

events.title: Håkon Wium Lie proposes CSS
events.summary: Håkon Wium Lie published Cascading HTML Style Sheets — a proposal on October 10, 1994 while at CERN.
events.about: CSS separated presentation from HTML structure — letting authors suggest fonts and layout while users could override styles. Every modern website still depends on the cascading model Lie proposed at CERN.

narrative.whyChosen: CSS is the presentation layer of the open web.
narrative.whyImportant: It ended the era of presentational HTML tags and font tags in markup.
narrative.problemSolved: Authors could not style pages consistently without polluting HTML with layout tags.

events.title: Tim Berners-Lee founds the W3C
events.summary: Tim Berners-Lee founded the World Wide Web Consortium on October 1, 1994 at MIT — stewarding web standards globally.
events.about: W3C standardized HTML, CSS, HTTP, and accessibility guidelines — keeping the web interoperable across browsers and devices. Berners-Lee led it without commercializing his invention.

narrative.whyChosen: W3C became the neutral forum for web standardization.
narrative.whyImportant: It prevented proprietary fragmentation of the open web.
narrative.problemSolved: Competing vendors needed a shared process to evolve web technologies.
